teaser: Who already insures AI agents, the four parts an insurer for behaviour policies needs, why capital matters, and why the first one starts as a managing agent.
core_idea: Several companies already sell AI agent cover but none we found prices per row of a behaviour policy; the insurance industry already separates the parts such a company needs (evidence, pricing and binding, the balance sheet, reinsurance), capital is the business for a carrier but not for a managing agent, so the first company can price on someone else's capital, start small, earn a loss record, and later carry the risk, with providers insuring their own agents and cover that lapses on unpatched known vulnerabilities.
